newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money nudges higher before weekend.
newsitem.headline: German call money nudges higher before weekend.

text.p: German overnight funds nudged fractionally higher on Friday as participants prepared for month-end.

Funds traded between 3.00/10 percent on Friday after trading between 3.00/02 percent on Thursday, when rates had already nudged slightly higher from the earlier session due to an anticipated jump in cash in circulation.
"Today's activities were coloured by the upcoming weekend and month-end early next week," a dealer said.
Another reason for the slight uptick in rates was that banks still needed to stock up some reserve holdings.
Dealers explained that since reserve holdings on Thursday had slipped to 44.6 billion marks compared with 46.7 billion marks on Wednesday rates ticked slightly higher.
Overall activity was slow however, dealers said, joking about the fact that the summer break has ebbed into the market.

Nonetheless dealers said they no longer believed that June's month end, which also marks half-year end, will be as smooth as they had thought earlier in the week. While rates had not jumped significantly at month end for some time, dealers now said they might well tick a bit higher this month.
Banks' average holdings for the month of June stood at 40.5 billion marks, which is still considered to be slightly below the required reserve target set by the Bundesbank.
Lombard borrowings were negligible on Thursday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Offered Rates FIONA= were set at 3.07733 percent on Friday compared with 3.03067 percent on Thursday.
